title: Incident Capacity Scarcity Response and SLO Tradeoffs — Quick Reference
content:
Purpose:
Quick, practical reference for cross-functional decisions when we face capacity scarcity (pool-wide GPU shortage, region outage, or supply-constrained maintenance) that could force temporary SLO relaxations or customer-facing throttles. Aim: give product, SRE, infra, support, and sales a shared decision surface and a minimal runbook to move quickly and consistently.

Scope / when to use this doc:
- Applies to incidents where capacity < 60% of nominal in a given region or dedicated pool for > 30 minutes.
- Focus is on model-serving capacity (GPU/accelerator pools) and associated latency/throughput SLOs.
- Not for complete control-plane outages (use full incident runbook).

High-level decision principles (simple):
1) Safety first: Prioritize critical enterprise customers with contractual SLAs and any real-time critical flows (billing, auth, safety checks).
2) Degrade predictably: Prefer controlled throughput/latency tradeoffs (rate limits, smaller batch sizes, graceful tail-latency targets) rather than random failures.
3) Short-lived concessions: Any SLO relaxation is timeboxed, observable, and reversible.
4) Communicate early: CS and Sales must get a templated update within 30 minutes of a capacity decision.

Stakeholder roles (one-liners):
- Eng-SRE (oncall): assess capacity, propose mitigation tier, enact runtime fallbacks, monitor metrics.
- Infra/Platform (capacity owners): validate hardware causes, surface ETA for reclaimed capacity.
- Product (hosting & dedicated product leads): decide customer priority, approve billing/compensation language.
- Support/CS: communication and customer triage for affected customers.
- Sales/Account Exec: coordinate with priority customers and negotiate temporary concessions.
- Legal: if contract changes or credits are proposed (only if > 24h impact).

Decision ladder (4-tier mitigation model) — choose the minimal tier required:
Tier 0 — Normal operation
- No action. Continue to monitor.

Tier 1 — Soft throttles and routing
- Actions: apply per-tenant burst caps, shift non-critical requests to fallback models (smaller/cheaper variant), enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Effect on SLOs: 2–5% increase in p95 latency possible, no formal SLA breach expected.
- Governance: SRE approves. Notify CS via short note.

Tier 2 — Targeted SLO relaxation + scheduled signals
- Actions: temporarily relax p99 latency target for non-enterprise routes, reduce batch windows to favor latency, enable reduced-token limits for best-effort customers.
- Effect on SLOs: p99 may degrade up to 30% for best-effort customers for up to 4 hours.
- Governance: Product + SRE approval. CS and Sales informed; prepare templated message.

Tier 3 — Capacity rationing (fair-share) + emergency routing
- Actions: enforce hard per-customer concurrency limits, enable fallbacks to hosted smaller-region replica, preempt non-critical workloads (background embeddings, re-ranking jobs), apply emergency auto-scale if reserved capacity exists.
- Effect on SLOs: Some customers will see reduced throughput; enterprise SLAs honored where possible.
- Governance: Exec oncall + Product + Infra sign-off. Customer credits considered per policy.

Tier 4 — Temporary SLO forbearance & customer remediation
- Actions: apply company-level mitigation: prioritize only SLA-backed traffic, queue/buffer non-critical requests, start customer credit assessment and legal review if > 4h outage.
- Effect on SLOs: Formal SLA impacts; escalate post-incident review.
- Governance: Exec leadership + Legal + Finance involved.

Quick tradeoff grid (decision knobs and typical consequences):
- Throughput cap (per-tenant concurrency): lowers peak tokens/sec, reduces global tail; consequence: increased queuing and client error rates if clients don't retry gracefully.
- Batch size reduction: reduces tail latency variability; consequence: higher per-token cost and lower throughput.
- Fallback to smaller model variant: reduces capacity pressure; consequence: potential quality regressions (monitor safety & eval prompts).
- Prefix/response caching: immediate relief for repeated prompts; consequence: cache-hit correctness concerns for personalized data — ensure opt-out flags.

Runbook (first 90 minutes) — checklist for oncall SRE:
T+0m — detection and triage
- Confirm capacity metrics (GPU utilization across pools, pending queue length, immediate failures).
- Post initial incident bridge with SRE, Infra, Product, CS (virtual room).

T+5–15m — rapid mitigations
- If capacity drop is localized: route traffic to healthy region if possible (check data residency constraints).
- If global: apply Tier 1 soft throttles + enable caching heuristics.

T+15–30m — targeted decisions
- Run the Tier decision ladder; record chosen tier and reason in incident doc.
- Prepare templated customer comm for affected cohorts (CS drafts; Sales identifies top-10 impacted accounts).

T+30–60m — stabilization
- If stabilized, start rolling back non-required mitigations iteratively.
- If not stabilized, escalate to Tier 3 and engage Product, Finance.

Communications templates (short):
- Internal (30m): "Capacity scarcity in us-west-2 impacting non-enterprise model-serving. Implemented Tier 1 throttles; p95 latency +3–6%. CS/Sales notified. SRE monitoring. ETA to re-evaluate: 30m. — Asha"
- Customer-facing (PSA, short): "We are experiencing reduced capacity in region X that may affect response times for some requests. We're prioritizing customers with contracted SLAs. We're actively mitigating and will share updates every 60 minutes."
- Top-account DM (private): include approximate impact, mitigation steps taken, expected ETA, and contact person.

Measurement & observability (must-haves):
- Dashboards: per-pool GPU util, queue size, p95/p99 latency per customer tier, error rates (5xx/429), cache-hit ratio, fallback-model percent.
- Alerts: capacity below 60% sustained for 15m; queue-length > threshold; fallback rate > 10%.
- Post-incident: run quality-sampling on fallback-model outputs for top impacted customers.

Experimentation playbook (fast probes we can run during or after):
- Short A/B on batch-size windows for one non-critical model to measure latency vs throughput impact (2-hour probe).
- Cache TTL tuning experiment for repeated prompt classes — measure true improvement and staleness risk.
- Quantization/quant-profile rollout test for one dedicated pool (lab only) to estimate capacity gain.

Open questions / decisions to surface to product committee:
- Compensation threshold: at what total downtime/quality delta do we auto-issue a customer credit? (current policy: 4+ hours non-SLA impact triggers review — propose 3h for model-serving?)
- Automated tier selection: can we safely encode the ladder into a policy (e.g., automatic Tier 1–2 triggers) or keep manual approvals?
- Safety checks for fallback models: do we need additional gating for safety-sensitive prompts?

Next steps (owners & short due-dates):
- SRE: add Tier alerts to the incident ops runbook and create a per-pool alert playbook (owner: Miguel; due: 2026-03-09).
- Product: draft temporary credit thresholds for review (owner: Emma; due: 2026-03-12).
- CS/Sales: build two templated messages (public PSA + top-account DM) and a roster for 24/7 coverage (owner: Noah; due: 2026-03-05).
- Infra: validate fast-evacuate routing playbooks and region failover checklist (owner: Priya; due: 2026-03-15).

Notes to self / informal scratchpad:
- Keep the language simple in customer PSAs; avoid engineering detail.
- We should simulate a 50% capacity event in the next chaos week and time the full decision ladder (TODO: schedule).
- Consider a 'grace token' feature that lets enterprise customers pre-authorize minor latency spikes without triggering crediting logic.

Appendix (links & quick refs):
- Capacity metrics dashboard (link to internal dashboard) — pinned to incident bridge.
- Customer priority matrix: (enterprise lists + contract tiers) — use for Tier decisions.

End of doc.

(Informal; iterative. This is intended to be a compact, action-oriented reference for SRE, Product, CS and Infra during capacity scarcity incidents. Replace owners/dates after triage.)
